exercise1.prompt: Two files, one question, and the checks that keep the answer honest.

hiddenCases.name: different files give a different answer
the two files are actually joined
hiddenCases.describe: both files read and merged on id

exercise1.hint: Read both, merge on id, group by team, take the mean of score, round it, then to_dict(). The second file set is different, so a typed-in answer fails.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a two-file analysis in the order this lesson recommends.
items: Load both files and look at them
Check the row count survived the join
questions.explain: The check sits between the join and the summary, because that is the point where a wrong join is still cheap to notice.

questions.prompt: Why check the row count after a join rather than before?
choices: The join is what changes it, by dropping or multiplying rows
questions.explain: Before the join there is nothing to compare against. The pair of numbers is what tells you which of the two failure modes you have.

questions.prompt: What does rounding the result at the end buy you?
choices: A number a reader can take in, with the working left exact until the last step
questions.explain: Rounding early loses precision through the calculation; rounding at the end is presentation.
